statement: Climate shifts the calendar: bloom, snow, monsoon, hurricane, seaweed, bleaching and harvest dates drift, so a 'best month' (a statement about the last few decades) slowly stops being true.
howToCheck: For this interest's five highest-rated places, compare the best months in our text with the last two seasons' conditions (national weather service or the relevant monitoring agency, and recent trip reports). Move the months and the curve where the pattern has shifted.

statement: Places are renamed, merged or redrawn. A rename leaks the old name into texts, and boundary changes break counts that were done for a circle or an administrative outline.
howToCheck: Run scripts/audit-old-rules.ts for this interest and read any old-name warning; search for renames or boundary changes among the interest's top places. Fix the text and re-check any count that used the old outline.

statement: Safety and politics change: war, unrest, disease and disasters change whether anyone should go. Those belong to the advisory layer, which is not built or filled yet.
howToCheck: Check the foreign-office advice for this interest's top places and recent news for anything that changes whether a visitor should go. Anything material goes into the advisories note for that place, and our text is caveated if needed.

statement: Money moves: fees, taxes, currency swings and inflation change what 'luxury', 'budget' or 'worth the price' mean, and entry and visa rules change who can go easily.
howToCheck: For this interest's top places, compare every price, fee or entry-rule claim in our text and columns with the official page (park authority, ministry or operator association). Update what changed.

statement: Overtourism controls arrive: caps, timed tickets, day-visitor fees and bans are being added in many popular places, and each changes what a visit is like.
howToCheck: Search the managing authorities of this interest's top places for new visitor caps, timed entry, day-visitor fees or bans, and update the practical wording.

statement: Transport and access change: a new airport, ferry, road, rail line or lift (or the loss of one) changes how reachable and how crowded a place is.
howToCheck: For this interest's top places, search for new or lost airports, ferry, rail and road links and lift openings in the last year, and update the access and crowding wording.

statement: Our own sources age: map data (Overture, released monthly), Wikidata, the climate figures (fixed windows), the English proficiency index, eBird, and lists such as Michelin and UNESCO are all snapshots, and a column built from one is correct only until the next release.
howToCheck: List the data sources behind this interest's columns (the Evidence lines say which) and check each source's latest release date against the date the column was built. Re-run the column's script where a newer release exists.

statement: Our own scale moves: every 10 is relative to the other places in the same interest, so adding or re-scoring places can make an older 10 unfair even if nothing about that place changed.
howToCheck: Re-read this interest's 10s and top ratings against the places added or re-scored since the last review, and move any that are no longer the top of their type. Needs your judgement on the scale.
